sheet-1-1.description: The main part of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, shows the industrial district south of Stanhope's centre, between Furnace Street and the Musconetcong River below Furnace Pond. Most of it is taken by the Musconetcong Iron Works and the Singer Sewing Machine Company. The iron works are drawn with a power house, blowing engines, double-deck boilers, a casting house, stoves and a long stock house with stock bins under tracks on trestles, with stone retaining walls along the furnace yard. The Singer Sewing Machine Company occupies the large concrete building of fireproof construction south of the iron works, with machine work, casting, cleaning and storage and shipping rooms; some of it is marked not used. West of it, along a railroad siding, stand the buildings of the United States Mineral Wool Company: chambers, a cupola, engine room, store houses, a store house lined with tin, a carpenter shop, sheds and a locomotive house. Railroad tracks and sidings cross the sheet from the left and fan out across the works, and the curving channel of the Musconetcong River runs through the left half of the part. Furnace Reservoir, fed from the canal, lies at the right edge, and Furnace Pond at the bottom. Notes give each plant's power, heating, lighting and fire protection. At the top right a short length of Furnace Street with two brick dwellings of block 17 continues Sheet 3. The legend and the location map of New Jersey printed on the left are cut out of the mask.
notes: Placed from two points carried from Sheet 3 (the front corners of the dwelling at 7-8 Furnace Street, drawn on both sheets), with the scale of Sheet 2 and north at 48 degrees taken from the same dwelling and Furnace Street on both sheets; the drawn north arrow points about 8 degrees further anticlockwise. Low confidence: errors grow away from the top right corner.
Modern Furnace Street runs north to south through the former works site; the 1920 Furnace Street is the short street at the top right.

sheet-1-2.description: This part, the top left quarter of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up, shows the east end of Main Street in Stanhope where it meets Reservoir Avenue, beside the Morris Canal and Lake Musconetcong. Reservoir Avenue runs up the middle of the part from a wooden bridge over the canal; Main Street runs in from the left edge to meet it. West of Reservoir Avenue on Main Street stand a motion picture theatre of iron-clad frame with a stage, a small shop and blacksmith shop, two brick stores and dwellings. East of the avenue are dwellings, one named Everbreeze, a small ice house and auto house, and the large E. T. Wills ice house, with an incline running down to the shore. Below Main Street the Morris Canal runs across the part, with a lock and lock house, and Lake Musconetcong fills the lower right and the right side of the part. A power and light company structure stands near the lock. Water pipes of six and eight inches are drawn along Main Street and Reservoir Avenue, the latter laid in 1913, and the street widths (50 feet for Main Street, 33 feet for Reservoir Avenue) are lettered. Block numbers 21, 22 and 23 mark the areas. The part is bounded on the right by the index and key map, which are not georeferenced.
notes: Reservoir Avenue is Ledgewood Avenue here today (US 46 / NJ 183); north of the fork it continues as Musconetcong Avenue.

sheet-1-3.description: An inset at the bottom left of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing Clarks Row in Stanhope from its junction with Brookland Avenue. Brookland Avenue, 33 feet wide, enters from the lower left corner and meets Clarks Row, which runs along the bottom edge of the inset; only the near side of Clarks Row is drawn. The block above it, number 25, holds a row of four frame double dwellings of two storeys facing Clarks Row, numbered 15 to 28, and a small stable behind them; the rest of the block is empty. The ground beyond Brookland Avenue is marked vacant. A six-inch water pipe runs along Clarks Row and a four-inch pipe along Brookland Avenue, with a hydrant at the corner. The inset is bounded above by a heavy line, beyond which the main map of the sheet shows the works along the Musconetcong River; the lettering No Exposure along that line marks that nothing on that side bears on these buildings.
notes: Brookland Avenue is Brooklyn Road (NJ 183) today; Clarks Row is the stretch of Ledgewood Avenue between High Street and Musconetcong Avenue.
Summit Street, which today crosses this block, is not drawn.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern part of central Stanhope, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left of the page. Main Street crosses the sheet from left to right through its middle, with Linden Avenue parallel to it near the top. Bedford Avenue runs down from Main Street at the left edge, turns along the bottom of the sheet and meets King Street, which runs from Main Street to the bottom edge. Church Street and New Street meet Main Street at the right edge, a few feet apart, and New Street bends away towards the lower right corner. The sheet is almost entirely residential: frame dwellings, most of one or two storeys, on long narrow lots, with outbuildings, sheds, auto houses and an ice house behind them. Large areas of the blocks are empty back land. Institutions are the Stanhope Public School, a brick building of two storeys heated by hot air, north of Linden Avenue; the Episcopal Church at Linden Avenue and Church Street; and the Presbyterian Church on Main Street near New Street. Commercial uses are few: the J. H. Phillips Milk Station with a concrete ice house and a bottling shed near New Street, and the Sunny Side Bakery with its ovens on Bedford Avenue near King Street. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along Main Street, Linden Avenue, Bedford Avenue and King Street, some dated 1904 and 1913, with hydrants at intervals. The lower left corner is marked vacant beyond Bedford Avenue. Street widths are lettered: 40 feet for Linden Avenue and Bedford Avenue, 30 to 36 feet for King, Church and New Streets.
notes: The leg of Bedford Avenue that runs from Main Street to the corner is Bell Street today; the leg along the bottom of the sheet is still Bedford Avenue.
King Street continues south of Bedford Avenue as Plane Street today.
Main Street and Linden Avenue are listed in OpenStreetMap as Main Street and Linden Avenue.
Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Main St, Linden Av, Bedford Av (left leg = Bell St today), King (continues as Plane St), Church, New. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the business centre of Stanhope and the streets south of it, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left of the page. Main Street enters from the left edge, where Church Street and New Street meet it, runs across the sheet and turns north-east to run beside the Morris Canal along the upper right. Linden Avenue runs along the top and curves up to meet High Street, which runs diagonally down to Main Street; Drive is a short street between High Street and Main Street. Below Main Street, New Street, Plane Street, Canal Street, Furnace Street and Hacketstown Road run diagonally towards the lower right. The commercial blocks along Main Street hold stores, a bakery, drugs and confectionery, a barber, shoe shop and news stand, a post office, a hall, the Franklin House and the Stanhope House hotels with hitching sheds, the Masonic Building, a lodge and club, a garage for 30 cars and auto supply stores. A former Methodist Episcopal church stands at Linden Avenue and Church Street. The Morris Canal with its canal basin and tow path runs up the right side; Plane No. 2 West, the canal's inclined plane, and a flume to the power house are drawn as parallel lines across the lower middle of the sheet, between Plane Street and Canal Street. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings on small lots, with the P. J. Kelly beer bottling works and the L. D. Kopferman ladies' underwear factory among them. Water pipes of four and six inches, hydrants and street widths of 30 to 48 feet are marked. The lower right corner continues on Sheet 1 (block 17 on Furnace Street).
notes: Upper Furnace Street and Hacketstown Road together are Kelly Place today; Canal Street is Plane View.
Main Street east of High Street and Drive have no counterpart junctions in OpenStreetMap that match the drawing (the area is an open square on the sheet); not used as control.
The drawn junction of Linden Avenue and High Street lies about 10 m from today's junction (Linden Avenue realigned at its end); not used as control.
Plane No. 2 West is the inclined plane of the Morris Canal, now the Morris Canal Greenway corridor.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Business centre: Main, Linden Av, Church, New, High, Drive, Plane, Canal (= Plane View), Furnace and Hacketstown Rd (= Kelly Place), Morris Canal and Canal Basin. One part.
